cover.alt: The round-up on the heath above Jökuldalur as morning fog lifts: Bjarni, Jón and Óli ride beside a flock of white and black sheep and lambs. Siggi and Ketill run in the foreground with two sheepdogs, and a rocky ravine with a stream stretches behind them.
cover.art_brief: Mid-September 1874 on the brown-and-rust heath above Jökuldalur. Morning fog is lifting in pale banks and the sun comes through. Two farmers ride and call at the left: broad, dark-bearded Bjarni, 44, on a large brown Icelandic horse, and lean, weathered Jón, about 40, grey-brown beard and sheepskin-coloured jacket, on a small grey horse. Tall red-bearded Óli, 24, in a cap and plain cream work jumper, rides a dark Icelandic horse a little behind them. Two sheepdogs run near the flock: cream-and-tan Snati, pointed ears and curled tail, and Jón's black-and-white dog. White and black Icelandic ewes with half-grown lambs move down the open slope, some bleating. At the right Siggi and Ketill run alongside the flock on firm heath ground; beyond their route a narrow rocky ravine with a thin stream at its bottom makes the two high sides and low water visible. Siggi is 11, thin, with tousled sandy hair, plain brown knitted work jumper, grey breeches and sewn sheepskin shoes. Ketill is 12, stockier, straight black hair under a dark knitted cap, patched dark-blue homespun jacket, grey breeches and sewn sheepskin shoes. These are five people total, with the two mounted farmers, the mounted farmhand and the two running boys clearly separated. The ravine is a background feature, away from the running boys' feet. Established Kafli 1–3 farm ink-and-watercolour style; plain period working clothes. No text, letters or numerals anywhere.

One white ewe stands on the ledge; beside her a frightened half-grown white lamb lies with its legs folded under its body, about half the ewe's size. Both animals are below both boys. Siggi and Ketill are descending the same rocky side from the upper rim toward the animal ledge. Each boy steadies himself with one hand on the rock while lowering one foot toward a clearly lower foothold, looking down toward the sheep below; their bent knees and downward-reaching feet make the direction clear. At the top, three distinct men stand on foot and call down with hands cupped at their mouths: Bjarni, 44, broad with dark beard; Jón, about 40, lean with grey-brown beard and sheepskin-coloured jacket; Óli, 24, tall and red-bearded in a cap and plain cream jumper. The frame contains these five people and the two sheep; the three men remain well above the boys. Siggi is 11, thin, tousled sandy hair, plain brown knitted work jumper, grey breeches and sewn sheepskin shoes. Ketill is 12, stockier, black hair under a dark knitted cap, patched dark-blue homespun jacket, grey breeches and sewn sheepskin shoes. inference_aids.label: mark
inference_aids.alt: Two upright ears rise from one shared woolly base. The left ear has its tip cut straight across; the right ear has two V-shaped notches along its outer edge and a small round hole near the tip.
inference_aids.art_brief: Spot vignette, 1:1, plain flat white background. Two separate Icelandic sheep's heads and upper necks, a larger white ewe on the left and a smaller white half-grown lamb on the right, with a clear empty gap between their heads. Each head has its own visible eye, muzzle, woolly neck and one broad sideways-projecting ear, so the ears clearly belong to two different animals. Show the two marked ears at comparable scale and angle in the foreground. The ewe's visible ear has its tip cut straight across, matching the established square-ended earmark. The lamb's visible ear has two clear V-shaped notches along its rear edge and a small round hole near the tip; its tip remains rounded. The difference must be obvious at margin size and must not resemble the single front-edge V-notch used for the other farmer's mark. Natural pale healed ear edges, no fresh blood. Ink-and-watercolour farm style. No tags, branding, text, names, letters or numerals.

words_with_history.title: Orð með sögu
text: Í dag eru göngur: mennirnir og hundarnir fara, og kindurnar koma.
Bjarni segir: „Göngur: kindurnar.“ Siggi segir: „Göngur: gil, lamb og Ketill!“
words_with_history.note_en: Göngur is the plural of ganga, 'a walk' (from the verb ganga, 'to walk'): the autumn round-up, when farmers and boys walked and rode the heaths for days to gather the sheep that had grazed there all summer. A fjallkóngur ('mountain king') led them. Next comes the sorting pen, réttir (Kafli 5).

grammar.title: kallar · kalla
grammar.rule: Ketill kallar · mennirnir kalla · Siggi vaknar · Ásta og Helga vakna · Hvað gerir kindin? — Hún stendur.

tables.caption: kalla, vakna, jarma, klifra: hann, hún, það -ar · þeir, þær, þau -a

grammar.note_en: For -ar verbs (kalla, vakna, jarma, klifra) in the present, talking about someone else (third person: he, she, it, a name): one person or thing (singular: hann, hún, það, Siggi, kindin) takes -ar: Siggi kallar 'Siggi calls'; more than one (plural: þeir, þær, þau, mennirnir) takes -a: mennirnir kalla 'the men call'. The -a form is also the dictionary form. Hvað gerir …? asks what one person or thing is doing (Hvað gerir lambið? 'What is the lamb doing?'); Hvað gera …? asks the same about more than one (Hvað gera strákarnir? 'What are the boys doing?').

provenance.prompt: textbook loop step write, attempt 20261026T035052642-is-kvold-01-write-c04; docs/icelandic-kvoldvaka-design.md §6 row 4; content/is/plan/chapters.json row 4
provenance.review_required: Codex cross-model language review and a fluent native review before the owner promotes the text
notes: Lexemes: the 26 of chapters.json row 4 exactly (24 words + the place chunks á heiðinni, í gilinu); budget 26, ceiling 28. No open slots (Hluti 1). Incidentals used (row incidental_allowed): hleypur, ríður (3sg of the new lexemes hlaupa, ríða), geltir (made transparent in the text by „Voff, voff!“), gerir, Komdu (form gloss komdu ← koma), and the 3pl of koma, fara, sofa, standa, hafa. hefur (hafa) is first met here at s012 („Hann hefur ekki átta fætur!“), moved from Kafli 3 at fix 20261027T031328857-is-kvold-01-fix (F002); like the other incidentals it rests on context, not a margin gloss, so it carries the same planned-gloss warning. heita, spyrja, lesa stay 3sg-only (spyr is used as a speech tag only).
G04 in the first third: the minimal pair is sentence 2 (Siggi vaknar … Ásta og Helga vakna ekki: þær sofa); kallar s013, kalla s022; Hvað gera …? s029, Hvað gerir …? s043, s045.

No accusative that differs from the nominative: objects are neuter, feminine plural or indefinite (sér það, hefur mark, hafa mark, á þessar kindur, á margar, segir lítið, segir það, átta fætur). í/á + dative only in the place chunks (á Jökuldal, á túninu, á heiðinni, í gilinu) and in Óðinn situr á Sleipni, which repeats Kafli 2 s055 (licensed at G02; Codex flagged it in both passes against the closed chunk list I gave it, and itself noted the G02 licence).

Text routes of the row used, adapted: ganga, á heiðinni, þoka (without a third 'Í dag'), hlaupa (afi), ríða (afi's Óðinn line), lamb (Kind og lamb koma: kindin er mamma, og lambið er barn), gil (+ the SVG at the same sentence), í gilinu, mark (in Óli's mouth, not a narrator question, + the earmark SVG), hræddur (the lamb and Snati), klifra.

seinn is introduced by Ketill's teasing „Hann er seinn!“ (s020, gloss fljótur ↔ seinn): Siggi in fact woke early, so the tease is a small joke and the start of the rivalry. stoltur rests on context (… en þeir eru stoltir: kindin er hér, og lambið er hér; Óli: „í dag eru strákarnir stórir menn!“; Ásta: „Siggi er stoltur, og Ketill er stoltur!“); no closed-list gloss fits it honestly, and English is not allowed in the margin. Codex rated it a blocker twice (proud vs happy/relieved); I judged the gist ('pleased with themselves, feeling grown') resolvable and left it as a review question.
kaldur carries a sound gloss kalt: «brrr!» plus the fog context; flagged for the reviewer.

Codex review (cx job 1025-211210-12945) changes: the lamb is no longer carried (a September lamb is about four months old and heavy): Siggi calls it up as Ketill calls the ewe; Þau koma ekki upp states the need for rescue; Snati fer after Siggi's „Nei, Snati!“; Óli announces his retelling („Ásta, hér er sagan“); bóndi contrasted with vinnumaður; the ewe's mark says „Bjarni“ and the lamb's says neither „Bjarni“ nor „Jón“ (pass 2), after an SVG of Bjarni's and Jón's marks; x3-2-4/5 rewritten so that only one choice fits; b1 accepts bændurnir; b8 no longer contradicts the hook.

Hook without genitive or accusative: Kindin hefur mark, og það segir „Bjarni“. Lambið hefur mark líka, en það segir ekki „Bjarni“, og það segir ekki „Jón“. Jón: „Skrítið mark.“; Ásta: „Er lambið skrítið, pabbi?“ — „Nei. Markið er skrítið.“; Siggi: „Hver á lambið, pabbi?“; last line En markið segir það ekki, answering Óli's „markið segir það“.
The ewe is Bjarni's (her mark says „Bjarni“); the lamb with her has a mark nobody knows, so it is a stray that followed her (continuity log).

Media: margin_vignette 3 (þoka, gil, mark; Hluti 1 expects 4–10, a checker warning): the row plans three, and two SVG diagrams carry the exact relations. The planned cover, scene and vignettes support but never carry meaning.

Checker warnings grammar-unlicensed for heiðinni and gilinu are the row's new place chunks (course-lists.json place_chunks from 4), not yet in course.json.place_chunks (course.json is the runner's); same situation as Kafli 3's í heyinu.
pronunciation_note: hv = kv with hvar, hvað, hver (all in the chapter), per the row's pronunciation_drip.

review_questions.quote: „Göngur í dag, afi! En það er kalt.“
review_questions.question: Natural as an excited boy's line ('Round-up today, afi!')? And is the margin sound gloss kalt: «brrr!» acceptable for an Icelandic reader?

review_questions.quote: „Óðinn situr á Sleipni: Óðinn ríður,“ segir afi. „Og nú ríður Bjarni líka!“
review_questions.question: Natural in afi's voice (teasing comparison), with ríða intransitive?

review_questions.quote: „Pabbi, hvar er Siggi?“ spyr Ketill. „Hann er seinn!“
review_questions.question: Does seinn read naturally as late/slow teasing while Siggi is absent, immediately before his arrival at s021?

review_questions.quote: Bændurnir ríða og kalla, og strákarnir og hundarnir hlaupa.
review_questions.question: Natural for the riders setting out, calling to the dogs?

review_questions.quote: Kind og lamb koma. Kindin er stór, en lambið er lítið.
review_questions.question: Revised 2026-11-04 after review: the old „kindin er mamma, og lambið er barn“ implied parentage, but the lamb is a stray (s063). Now size contrast plus the define gloss „lamb: lítil kind“. Natural?

review_questions.quote: „Bjarni á margar, og Jón á margar líka,“ segir Óli. „Kindurnar hafa mark, og markið segir það.“
review_questions.question: Does markið segir það read as 'the mark tells (whose they are)'?

review_questions.quote: Þrír menn standa uppi og kalla niður.
review_questions.question: Is kalla niður natural for 'call down (into the ravine)'?

review_questions.quote: „Komdu, lamb! Komdu!“ kallar Siggi, og lambið kemur líka.
review_questions.question: Plausible that a half-grown lamb follows the ewe up when called, with the boys climbing beside them?

review_questions.quote: „Ásta, hér er sagan,“ segir Óli. „Kindin og lambið eru niðri í gilinu, og tveir strákar klifra niður! Þetta eru göngur, og í dag eru strákarnir stórir menn!“
review_questions.question: Óli retells in the present (historic present of oral storytelling), announced by „Ásta, hér er sagan“: natural? And „Þetta eru göngur, og í dag eru strákarnir stórir menn!“?

review_questions.quote: Strákarnir eru seinir, blautir og kaldir, en stoltir: kindin og lambið eru hér.
review_questions.question: Is stoltir resolvable from the reason clause and Óli's „í dag eru strákarnir stórir menn“, and natural?

review_questions.quote: Bjarni segir lítið. Hann sér lambið.
review_questions.question: Natural for 'Bjarni says little'?

review_questions.quote: Kindin hefur mark: „Bjarni“. Lambið hefur mark líka, en það segir ekki „Bjarni“, ekki „Jón“.
review_questions.question: Does the ewe's earmark followed by „Bjarni“ clearly convey ownership, and the lamb's contrasting mark its unknown owner? Is a lamb whose mark differs from the ewe it follows plausible (a stray)?
Does the last line read as 'but the mark doesn't tell (whose it is)'?
